svg.text: Step 4: the MAX485 module on the second board
Voltage divider on the lower half of the mini breadboard (rows f–j) · the second board's USB unplugged while wiring
↑ upper half (rows a–e): Module 9's battery circuit, not touched and not drawn
Faded wires = Module 14 wires that stay connected (Node 2's sensors, the board's 3V3 on rail + 29, its GND on rail − 28).
Wiring map: MAX485 module ↔ second board
The two direct wires (female–female) are drawn in full; the other wire ends are marked with their holes in the top panel.
USB to the laptop: plug in after the wiring is done
Node 2's sensor wires (Module 14) can stay connected; not drawn
Mini breadboard: RO → 14f · 4.7 kΩ 14h → 18h · 10 kΩ 18i → 22i · black 22j → bottom rail (−) 22 · 18f → board pin RX2
DE → 24f · RE → 24g · 24i → board pin D4 · DI → pin TX2 and VCC → pin VIN (female–female) · module GND → bottom rail (−) 23
Mini breadboard bottom rail (−) = the board's GND (Module 14's black wire). DON'T use the top rail: the board's GND wire to the battery circuit is removed.
